question: Can something a knot has by the growth law itself, in its own places, be one step on from what its parents have, so that the order of descent that births made one at a time need is shown by the structure? The note argues: under the recorded laws, no (a structure reached by a birth can be handed in again as a start, and then carries two records); under a ration written for it, yes, at one holder step, from a start whose meeting knots already agree and where parents' parent steps agree counted in threes, which moves the supplied record into the law and does not remove it. The run checks the note with a second program.
inputs: The starts, the laws with their three forms of the ration, the registered numberings, the hand cases and the two witness starts named in the pre-registration and its data files; the note and this study's definitions; the shared definitions of RING-IN-BALANCE-20261123-001; the core of the least-record study's engine and the knot tests named in the pre-registration, imported unchanged; the least-record study's record of its sixteen holding runs as a gate.
forbidden_inputs: Any definition changed after a value is seen; for the engine's author, the drafter's scratch prototype and anything it produced beyond what the pre-registration, the note and the data files disclose; any change to an imported engine or to another study's record.
primary_observable: For every registered run: where the place rule (the other holder of a shared place is a parent exactly when its count is one less, counted in threes) is right and where it is wrong, against the conditions the note states; on the census, the starts on which a new knot has parents at different numbers of parent steps, by law, with the splits the pre-registration lists; the starts of the census that are structures reached from a smaller census start, split into those after a complete round and the rest; the restart control; the ten lone-knot renamings; whether the births under the barred forms are the base law's; two rings with descent checked and the period read; the knot test of the structures named.
comparators_or_controls: The hand cases birth by birth; a planted error that must change exactly the predicted verdicts; the least-record study's sixteen holding runs reproduced; the two witness starts written out; the labelled weighting as the swap of the census weighting; counting in fives; the swap for parents whose counts differ; the earlier reading of a closing birth, reported as failing the knot test.
resource_budget: About twenty-five minutes in all on at most 6 processes, each under a memory cap, parts in the registered order; a part not finished within its registered size is cut to its prefix and what was not run is reported as not run.
first_executable_signal: The checks of part 0: the gate against the imported core, the hand cases birth by birth, the planted error, the sixteen holding runs reproduced, and the two witness starts.
decision_rule: Each prediction is judged by its 'Fails when' entry. Every prediction was written after the drafter's scratch runs and is marked as a check of the code, a replication of scratch, or by argument; none is counted as a new finding.
stop_rule: Stop when every registered part is done in its registered order or reported as cut, and every prediction has a verdict.
nonclaims: A note of two arguments, neither refereed, with one confirming run; everything in it was seen in scratch before it was written. The ration that writes the count is a rule of the law: no pattern counts, nothing but the ration uses the count, no birth depends on the comparison, and nothing here is a clock. The result is 'shown in the structure's places; written by the law; relative to a start supplied flat': the supplied record is moved, not removed. It does not show that no law without such a rule could show the order from a class of starts stated without it. No claim about physical time.
